result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick a 4px base with a 1.2 ratio and give values a developer could build from. B handles Tailwind better: it keeps Tailwind's 4px spacing but rejects its default type sizes as too small for gloved use. B's reasoning also matches its own numbers, and it adds row heights, line heights and a token table with intended uses. A's per-device type scales are a clean way to handle desktop vs tablet, but it argues for 28/36px rows and then specifies 32px rows, and its take on Tailwind is thinner. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers choose 4px with a 1.2 ratio and give numbers a developer could build from. B handles the desktop/tablet tension more cleanly: it defines two complete type scales under the same token names, keeps a short spacing list, and sets a 16px minimum for tablet data text. A mixes a touch-target size into its spacing tokens and only hints at how body text maps per device. B's 'don't go below 48px' line slightly muddies its 56px minimum, and A treats Tailwind a little more fully.
